Optional: when omitted, the organization's configured default data center is used (maintained by the platform administrator); if the organization has no default configured, the request returns 400. If the effective data center is under maintenance, the request returns 409 `IDC.UnderMaintenance`. Note that Templates are bound to a data center: the effective data center (whether explicit or default) must match the one that owns the Template or snapshot referenced by the request, otherwise a Template is reported as not found (400 `Parameter.Invalid`); a snapshot that exists but belongs to another data center also returns 400 `Parameter.Invalid` (404 `Resource.NotFound` is returned only when the snapshot does not exist).

secure.description: Enables traffic-access-token authentication on the user endpoint.

template_id.description: Template identifier or name. Mutually exclusive with snapshot_id: both or neither returns 400 `Sandbox.SourceConflict`. A template that cannot be found in the effective IDC returns 400 `Parameter.Invalid`.

cwd.description: Working directory the command runs in (relative paths in the command resolve against it). It must be absolute and normalized: no `.`, `..` or empty segments (a trailing `/` is normalized away); otherwise 400 `Execution.InvalidRequest`. When omitted, defaults to the template's working directory (the image or Dockerfile WORKDIR; depends on the template and IDC, for example `/` or `/home/user`; pass `cwd` explicitly when it matters). If the directory does not exist the execution ends with status `failed` and `failure_reason` `cwd_not_found`. If the path exists but is not a directory the execution ends with `failed` and `failure_reason` `cwd_not_directory`.

envs.description: Environment variables for the command. Names must be valid environment variable names (letters, digits and underscore, not starting with a digit) of at most 128 bytes, and each value is at most 64 KiB; otherwise the request returns 400 `Execution.InvalidRequest`.

execution_timeout_seconds.description: Time limit for this command, in seconds. When the limit is reached the command is terminated (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after a grace period) and the execution ends with status `timed_out` and a null `exit_code`. A value outside 1..3600 returns 400. This is unrelated to `wait_timeout_seconds`, which only bounds how long the request waits for a result. A command stopped this way reports `termination_reason` `execution_timeout`.

operations.name: create-template

allOf.description:
Initial Build definition used only by the combined Template-create
flow. A file context cannot be attached until the Template has a stable
ID; use the split create/upload/start flow when files are required.

build_timeout_sec.description:
Wall-clock budget for this Build in seconds. Omit or null to use the
platform default (600). Allowed range: 60–3600. On expiry the Build
is finalized as `error` with failure code `TemplateBuild.TimedOut`,
its backing build in the selected IDC is cancelled, and its partial
artifacts are reclaimed, best-effort.

commands.description:
Shell command strings executed sequentially during the Build. They may
run as a non-root account with passwordless sudo: prefix privileged
commands with `sudo`, and set ownership of files that the runtime
account must use. To control the build identity explicitly, use a
Dockerfile source with `USER` instructions, as in a regular Dockerfile.

default_user.description:
Runtime default identity for Sandboxes launched from this Build.
Without it, Sandboxes run as `docker run` would: as the Dockerfile's final
USER, else the image's USER, else root, in the final WORKDIR, else the
image's, else `/`.
Sandboxes run commands as a named account: an image USER given as a
numeric uid (or uid:gid) needs a matching /etc/passwd entry in the image,
otherwise the Build fails with a reason that names the USER. The group
part is ignored.
It is applied after all build commands and overrides the final Dockerfile
USER at runtime; it does not change the identity of earlier build commands.

Recommended setup for a custom account: create it in the Dockerfile, give
it a working directory it can access, and pass its uid, for example
`RUN useradd --uid 9999 --create-home --shell /bin/bash app`,
`WORKDIR /home/app`, and `default_user: {username: app, uid: 9999}`.

- default_user changes the identity only, not the working directory or its
  permissions. If the account cannot enter the final working directory,
  commands cannot start there and the Build may fail; declare an
  accessible WORKDIR to fix it.
- With uid, the account must already exist with that UID and an existing
  home directory; otherwise the Build fails. The platform does not change
  UID, ownership, groups, or sudo privileges.
- A non-root username without uid may be rejected with HTTP 422
  (Template.ProviderNotSupported); supply uid to avoid this. root may omit uid.
- Invalid username, out-of-range uid, or root with a nonzero uid returns
  HTTP 400 (Parameter.Invalid).
- A Build from a base template keeps the base template's user and working
  directory, as Docker FROM does; set default_user on the child Build to
  select another. Changing it requires a new Build.

When omitted, the template's default runtime identity is used. A Build
response reports the requested setting; an omitted uid stays omitted.

uid.description: UID of the account. Recommended for non-root usernames. root only accepts 0.

envs.description: Build-only environment variables; values are write-only.

source.description: Manual Build source. Sandbox sources use the snapshot endpoint.

image.description:
OCI container image reference. The following distributions have
been validated: Debian/Ubuntu, Fedora/CentOS Stream/Rocky Linux/
AlmaLinux, Arch Linux, and Alpine Linux.

registry_credential.description: A one-time registry credential used to pull the private image named by `image`. `username` and `password` are used only for this build request: they are never persisted and never returned in any response. The Build detail's `registry_authentication` reports only whether a credential was used and of what kind, never the username or password.

password.description: Can be a password or an access token.

build_id.description:
Optional parent Build identifier. When omitted, the parent's
current successful Build is used.

template_id.description: Parent GMI Template identifier in the same IDC.

dockerfile.description:
Raw Dockerfile text. Supported instructions: FROM (exactly one; no
multi-stage), RUN, ENV, WORKDIR, USER, COPY/ADD, CMD/ENTRYPOINT;
EXPOSE and VOLUME are skipped; anything else is rejected with 400.

A trailing backslash continues an instruction on the next line; blank
and comment lines inside a continuation are skipped.

The Dockerfile's final USER is the runtime identity of Sandboxes unless
`default_user` is set. A Build fails when that account cannot enter the
final working directory; declare an accessible WORKDIR.

COPY/ADD sources must reference an uploaded Template file as
`COPY {{file:<file_id>}} /dest` — local paths and URLs are
rejected, and at most one file may be referenced per build (its
`file_id` must also be attached via `file_context`, with
`file_context.destination` omitted).

With a dockerfile source, the sibling `commands` and `envs` fields
are forbidden: write RUN/ENV lines in the Dockerfile instead.
CMD/ENTRYPOINT are extracted into the Build's start command; an
explicit `start_cmd` takes precedence over them.

ENV values are visible to subsequent build steps and are part of
the sandbox runtime environment, as under `docker run`; a value
passed as `env_vars` when creating a Sandbox overrides one of the
same name. Do not put build-time secrets in ENV: build the Template
from an image or template source and pass them in `envs`, which
reach the build steps only.

start_cmd.description: Launch command applied when Sandboxes from this Template start.

build.description:
Initial Build definition created and started with the Template
(combined flow, every IDC supports it). A `file_context` cannot be
attached here; use the split flow when files are required. Omitting
`build` selects the split flow: the Template and a `waiting`
initial Build are created without starting anything, and the Build
is started later via `POST /templates/{template_id}/builds/{id}`.
The split flow is not supported in every IDC; unsupported IDCs
reject it with 422.

idc_name.description: IDC that permanently owns the Template. Optional: omitted, empty, and whitespace-only values are equivalent — the organization's configured default data center is used (maintained by the platform administrator; the same setting used by sandbox creation). If the organization has no default configured, the request returns 400. If the effective data center is under maintenance, the request returns 409 `IDC.UnderMaintenance`.

product.description:
Sandbox product specification id (catalog SKU, for example
`gmi.sandbox.x-large`).

resources.description:
Resource values are selected by catalog product SKU
(`GET /api/v2/products`); the service resolves the active entry from
the product catalog.

`file_id` must also be attached via `file_context`, with
`file_context.destination` omitted).

With a dockerfile source, the sibling `commands` and `envs` fields
are forbidden: write RUN/ENV lines in the Dockerfile instead.
CMD/ENTRYPOINT are extracted into the Build's start command; an
explicit `start_cmd` takes precedence over them.

the sandbox runtime environment, as under `docker run`; a value
passed as `env_vars` when creating a Sandbox overrides one of the
same name. Do not put build-time secrets in ENV: build the Template
from an image or template source and pass them in `envs`, which
reach the build steps only.

start_cmd.description:
Launch command persisted with the Build and applied when Sandboxes
created from this Template start.

It runs as a boot script before the sandbox's main process, and the
sandbox only becomes ready once it returns, so the command must
terminate. A foreground long-running command (`sleep infinity`, a
server started in the foreground) leaves the Sandbox stuck
initializing and every exec against it rejected.

Appending `&` alone is not sufficient: a backgrounded process that
still holds the inherited stdout/stderr keeps boot blocked just the
same. Long-running processes must be backgrounded *and* detached
from those streams, e.g.
`my-server > /var/log/my-server.log 2>&1 &`.

build_timeout_sec.description:
Wall-clock budget for this Build in seconds. Omit or null to use the
platform default (600). Allowed range: 60–3600. On expiry the Build
is finalized as `error` with failure code `TemplateBuild.TimedOut`,
its backing build in the selected IDC is cancelled, and its partial
artifacts are reclaimed, best-effort.

commands.description:
Shell command strings executed sequentially during the Build. They may
run as a non-root account with passwordless sudo: prefix privileged
commands with `sudo`, and set ownership of files that the runtime
account must use. To control the build identity explicitly, use a
Dockerfile source with `USER` instructions, as in a regular Dockerfile.

default_user.description:
Runtime default identity for Sandboxes launched from this Build.
Without it, Sandboxes run as `docker run` would: as the Dockerfile's final
USER, else the image's USER, else root, in the final WORKDIR, else the
image's, else `/`.
Sandboxes run commands as a named account: an image USER given as a
numeric uid (or uid:gid) needs a matching /etc/passwd entry in the image,
otherwise the Build fails with a reason that names the USER. The group
part is ignored.
It is applied after all build commands and overrides the final Dockerfile
USER at runtime; it does not change the identity of earlier build commands.

Recommended setup for a custom account: create it in the Dockerfile, give
it a working directory it can access, and pass its uid, for example
`RUN useradd --uid 9999 --create-home --shell /bin/bash app`,
`WORKDIR /home/app`, and `default_user: {username: app, uid: 9999}`.

- default_user changes the identity only, not the working directory or its
  permissions. If the account cannot enter the final working directory,
  commands cannot start there and the Build may fail; declare an
  accessible WORKDIR to fix it.
- With uid, the account must already exist with that UID and an existing
  home directory; otherwise the Build fails. The platform does not change
  UID, ownership, groups, or sudo privileges.
- A non-root username without uid may be rejected with HTTP 422
  (Template.ProviderNotSupported); supply uid to avoid this. root may omit uid.
- Invalid username, out-of-range uid, or root with a nonzero uid returns
  HTTP 400 (Parameter.Invalid).
- A Build from a base template keeps the base template's user and working
  directory, as Docker FROM does; set default_user on the child Build to
  select another. Changing it requires a new Build.

When omitted, the template's default runtime identity is used. A Build
response reports the requested setting; an omitted uid stays omitted.

uid.description: UID of the account. Recommended for non-root usernames. root only accepts 0.

envs.description:
Environment variables available only during the Template Build.
They are visible to subsequent build commands/steps and are not persisted
into the resulting template artifact as sandbox runtime environment
variables. Pass runtime env when creating a Sandbox instead. Write-only:
values are never returned on Template or TemplateBuild responses.
Keys must be unique (JSON object); the server orders them
deterministically by key. Key names must match
`[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`.

destination.description:
Absolute destination copied from the archive root during the Build.
Required for image/template sources; forbidden for a dockerfile
source, whose `COPY {{file:...}} /dest` lines carry their own
destinations.

file_id.description: GMI file identifier returned by the upload initialization endpoint.

source.description: Manual Build source. Sandbox sources use the snapshot endpoint.

image.description:
OCI container image reference. The following distributions have
been validated: Debian/Ubuntu, Fedora/CentOS Stream/Rocky Linux/
AlmaLinux, Arch Linux, and Alpine Linux.

registry_credential.description: A one-time registry credential used to pull the private image named by `image`. `username` and `password` are used only for this build request: they are never persisted and never returned in any response. The Build detail's `registry_authentication` reports only whether a credential was used and of what kind, never the username or password.

password.description: Can be a password or an access token.

build_id.description:
Optional parent Build identifier. When omitted, the parent's
current successful Build is used.

template_id.description: Parent GMI Template identifier in the same IDC.

dockerfile.description:

A trailing backslash continues an instruction on the next line; blank
and comment lines inside a continuation are skipped.
